title: Graph revision supersession transition
description: Objective: compose the sibling core supersession decision kernel into the graph-revision aggregate so `graph.supersede` becomes the only authority-moving transition from ACTIVE, with durable graph epochs and an atomic predecessor/successor binding. Deliverable: update graph-revision contract, validation, result shaping, reducer, deterministic fixtures, reducer tests, invariant command drivers, and the active-revision invariant test. The command must carry predecessor epoch plus explicit successor identity/content/epoch/carry evidence; ACTIVE state persists the current epoch; the accepted result atomically marks the predecessor SUPERSEDED and emits the hash-bound successor activation decision. Exact dependency on the kernel child created in this split will be recorded in a task comment. NOT in scope: implementing carry policy/disposition hashing itself, scheduler attempt/effect/resource/budget application, daemon persistence, UI, or changing unrelated lifecycle assertions. Owned paths: packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts, graph-revision-validation.ts, graph-revision-results.ts, graph-revision-reducer.ts, graph-revision-test-fixtures.ts, graph-revision-reducer.test.ts, planning-invariant-drivers.ts, planning-invariants.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: `GraphRevisionState` carries a required validated graph epoch, initial activation establishes epoch 1, and `GraphRevisionSupersedeCommand` carries an explicit predecessor/successor epoch and kernel decision input rather than a refusal witness.

`GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS` admits `graph.supersede` from ACTIVE only; a valid current-epoch command invokes the production kernel, marks the predecessor SUPERSEDED, and emits one frozen atomic event/result binding the successor ACTIVE at exactly predecessor epoch + 1.

Stale/rebound epoch or successor identity refuses with exact `REVISION_REBOUND` at `GRAPH_REVISION`; changed or UNKNOWN carry evidence refuses with exact `SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED` at `GRAPH_REVISION`; every further command against SUPERSEDED refuses with exact `SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY` at `GRAPH_REVISION`, leaving input state byte-identical.

`graph-revision-reducer.test.ts` replaces only assertions invalidated by the real supersede transition, while fixtures and the planning invariant test stop treating a well-formed supersede as universally illegal; generated lifecycle/command sweeps assert a positive case count and exact code/layer.
Mutation drills make the epoch equality, +1 successor epoch, predecessor hash binding, UNKNOWN/changed carry invalidation, and superseded guard tests fail when each production guard is weakened.

Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0, all eight owned files are the only committed paths, and every production source remains at or below 250 physical lines.
taskRails: Depends on the sibling core supersession decision-kernel child from this split; consume that production surface rather than reimplementing epoch/carry/disposition policy in reducer code or test helpers.
TDD every changed transition. Refusal assertions pin exact stable code and `GRAPH_REVISION` layer; generated sweeps assert non-zero case counts and exercise the production reducer.
Keep graphEpoch required and durable rather than optional or inferred from per-revision version; missing/UNKNOWN authority or input evidence fails closed.
Change only supersession-invalidated assertions in existing reducer/invariant suites; unrelated lifecycle and concurrency assertions must pass unchanged.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; stage/commit only the eight owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Contract. In graph-revision-contract.ts: (1) add `readonly graphEpoch: number` to GraphRevisionState. Semantics, pin them in a doc comment: this is a BOUND REFERENCE to the goal-owned epoch at which this revision was activated, not a private counter — that wording resolves the standing note at reducer.ts:5-7 which says epoch authority lives in the goal aggregate. Rule: graphEpoch >= 1 exactly when lifecycle is ACTIVE or SUPERSEDED, and exactly 0 otherwise. (2) Replace GraphRevisionSupersedeCommand's `witness: GraphRevisionRefusalWitness` with `readonly supersession: SupersessionInput`, importing the type from ../supersession/supersession-engine.js (no cycle: supersession imports only ../policy). Delete the stale '/** Replacement supersession is Phase 5 (design section 10); every preview entry is refused. */' comment at :76 — it is now false. (3) Add `GraphRevisionSuperseded extends GraphRevisionEventBase` with `readonly authorityHash: string`, `readonly kind: "GraphRevisionSuperseded"`, `readonly successor: SupersessionSuccessorBinding`, and add it to the GraphRevisionEvent union. (4) Add `readonly layer: typeof GRAPH_REVISION_LAYER` to GraphRevisionRejectedResult. This field is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: RuntimeError at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-factory.ts:20-31 has NO `source` field — createRuntimeError validates `source` then drops it — and REVISION_REBOUND and SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED both carry NO_KEY required detail keys (runtime-error-registry.ts:131-137), so without this discriminant the refusing layer is unobservable and DoD 3 is untestable. Budget ~25 lines against 94 free.

implementationPlan.description: The transition itself, in graph-revision-reducer.ts. (1) GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS: change `"graph.supersede": Object.freeze([])` to `Object.freeze(["ACTIVE"])`. (2) Remove "graph.supersede" from the shared illegal() case at :170 and route it to a new supersede() handler. (3) supersede(state, command) composes the production kernel and adds NO policy of its own: call decideSupersession({ graphContentHash: state.graphContentHash, graphEpoch: state.graphEpoch, revisionId: state.revisionId }, command.supersession). The kernel takes `unknown` and fully validates the input, so the reducer must NOT pre-validate the supersession payload — that would be the reimplementation task rail 1 forbids. On !ok return supersessionRefused(state, result.code) — this is where SUPERSESSION_KERNEL becomes GRAPH_REVISION. On ok, clonedState to lifecycle SUPERSEDED with version + 1, keeping graphEpoch unchanged (the predecessor keeps the epoch it was activated at; the successor's epoch+1 travels in the event binding, not in this aggregate's state), and emit one deep-frozen GraphRevisionSuperseded event. (4) In decide(), set graphEpoch: 1 on the ACTIVE clone so initial activation establishes epoch 1, and leave every pre-active clone at 0. (5) Rewrite the header comment at :5-11 so it states the new truth: the epoch is still goal-owned authority, and this aggregate now persists the bound epoch it was activated at so supersession can bind predecessor to successor. Leave the SUPERSEDED guard at :196 untouched — it already satisfies the terminal half of DoD 3. Line budget: 206 measured + ~18 = ~224, under 250; if it lands over, split the handler into a new file rather than shortening the guard.

1. LINE CEILING IS THE TIGHTEST CONSTRAINT. planning-source-size.test.ts enforces 250 physical lines on EVERY .ts in src/planning with no allowlist — tests, fixtures and drivers included. Headroom measured: invariant-drivers 235 (15 free), reducer.test 222 (28 free), reducer 206 (44 free). Step 9 names the escape hatch for drivers (move the builder into invariant-fixtures, 162 free). Measure with `grep -c ''`; PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and will lie in the optimistic direction.

2. EXACTLY 10 DISTINCT FILES, AT THE HARD CAP. planning-invariant-fixtures.ts is an expansion beyond the task's stated 8 owned paths, justified by the measurement in step 9. There is no room for an eleventh — if the work grows, report_blocked for a split rather than quietly writing an unowned path.

3. THE VACUITY TRAP IS THE MOST LIKELY WAY THIS TASK PASSES WHILE FAILING. Both loop assertions being edited (reducer.test.ts:143-151 and planning-invariants.test.ts:114-128) can be made green by simply excluding graph.supersede from the loop. That leaves supersede untested by those files and the suite green. Every exclusion must be paired with an immediate positive assertion. Likewise the driver's supersede body: leave it malformed and the whole random-walk suite stays green having never once reached SUPERSEDED.

4. LAYER RE-SHAPING IS EASY TO GET WRONG SILENTLY. The kernel returns layer SUPERSESSION_KERNEL; DoD 3 requires GRAPH_REVISION. Passing the kernel refusal through unmapped still returns the right CODE, so a test asserting only the code stays green. Drill (d) exists specifically to prove the layer assertion is live.

5. WRONG SOURCE DEGRADES SILENTLY. createRuntimeError fails closed to UNKNOWN_ERROR on a source the descriptor does not list. A refusal built with the wrong aggregate returns UNKNOWN_ERROR, not an exception — so assert the exact code, never merely ok===false.

6. SHARED WORKTREE. All agents work in one directory. `git diff` cannot see the new untracked test file, so never verify a mutation restore by an empty diff — hash the file. A foreign whole-tree completion hook may commit your in-progress bytes; if that happens do not amend, reset or stash (epic rail 3) — report the base-ref diff over your owned paths instead. Foreign repo-wide red (the known scheduler package-boundary shebang failure) is disclosed verbatim under the path-attribution rule, but your own owned-package legs must still be exit 0.

7. DISCLOSED DESIGN GAP, not a defect to fix here: activation sets graphEpoch to 1 literally, so a successor revision's own activation does not yet land at predecessor epoch + 1. DoD 2 asks only that the supersede result EMIT that binding, which this plan does. Closing the successor's own activation belongs to task-069853689ed643988cfec2d689f7edb7.
